name: C1808

origin.basis: CST is the Cheng Shin (正新) brand of Taiwan's Cheng Shin Rubber; China listings give the brand as CST/正新.

manufacturing.basis: The listing does not state the factory; Cheng Shin also makes bicycle tires at a mainland plant.

positioning: CST folding 120 TPI training clincher with a dual compound and puncture layer.
weight_basis: The listing gives one 225 g weight without a size, so no size weight is recorded.

community.summary: A commenter says a C1808 bought for CNY 70 lasted 15,000 km with fewer cracks than a pricier race tire, worn mostly by steep descents.

availability.note: Sold by Tmall and Taobao shops; no official CST store listing was read for this model.

price_observations.market: 东之耀运动户外专营店 (Tmall)
price_observations.conditions: Tmall list price before discounts on 2026-11-01 for the 28C folding option; coupon price CNY 92.25. Single or pair not stated.

caveats: One owner comparison only; no lab test found.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Checked on 2026-11-03: keyed Xiaohongshu evidence from bounded searches (the first 16-20 result cards of each query, opened exact posts and their visible comments; not exhaustive), coded owner by owner, plus the Sigma Sports and bike-components catalogues and Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test index. Counted only owners who describe their own riding of this model; questions, seller and maker replies, unmounted impressions and reports about other models were left out. Puncture and wear rankings that one owner inferred from materials are not counted as observed.

reports.summary: In an uncontrolled four-tire comparison of budget clinchers at 85/90 psi it ranked second for rolling and grip; no puncture occurred, so its protection was not observed.
After buying it: average overall and noisy, but its puncture protection is fine.
Fine in use so far, though not yet ridden on rough roads.
The bike's original tire: some small wear pits and a pinch cut on the side after a year, but never a flat.
Reported one flat at the front and one at the rear.
Easy to remove, but punctures easily: five flats in its worst month.
